conversation.Statement: Hello, this is Karen from Amazon Customer Care. Am I speaking with Mrs. Linda Matthews?
Yes, this is Linda.

Thank you, Mrs. Matthews. I'm reaching out regarding a recent issue on your Amazon account. There appears to be an unfamiliar subscription charge pending. Have you authorized any new services recently?
No, I haven't. I don't really use my Amazon much except to order gifts for my grandchildren.

I understand, and I want to assure you we're here to protect your account. I can see a $119.99 Prime Video subscription about to renew. Let's double check your details so we can get this sorted, all right?
Okay, yes. I'm on a fixed income, so I can't afford any extra charges.
Of course, Mrs. Matthews. Just to verify for your security, could you confirm the billing address associated with your Amazon account?
It should be 428 Maple Lane, Springfield, Ohio.
Thank you. Now, I'm looking at your account and I see some unusual login activity, possibly from another state. Have you traveled recently or shared your password with anyone?
No, it's just me. I haven't gone anywhere.
That's concerning. For your safety, we'll need to temporarily secure your account and process a cancellation for this subscription. Do you have access to your computer or smartphone right now?
Yes, my laptop is on.
Wonderful. I'll walk you through a quick verification step. Please open your internet browser and go to www.amazonhelpsecure.com.
Alright, it's loading. Is this part of Amazon?
Absolutely, this is our secure customer support portal. We use it for sensitive cases like yours. Please let me know when you see the blue login screen.
I see it now.
Perfect. Please enter your Amazon username and password so I can verify your account and prevent any unauthorized charges.
Okay, I've typed them in.

Thank you, Mrs. Matthews. Give me just a moment to check the information. Oh! I actually see a refund for $299 is pending to your account, but it looks like it's being sent to a different bank. Did you request a refund recently?
No, I haven't ordered anything that needed a refund.

That's what I suspected. It seems your account was compromised, and someone may have changed your refund method. To stop this, I'll need you to verify your current bank account number so we can redirect the refund to you.
Uh, it's 108542961 at First State Bank.

Thank you. To finalize the refund back to you, we use an Amazon gift card system for quick transfers. Can you please purchase three $100 Amazon gift cards from a nearby store? I'll provide instructions so we can process your refund and secure your funds.
I need to buy gift cards? Why can't you just put the money back in my bank account?

I completely understand your concern. Due to the suspicious activity, our policy requires us to use this method for your protection. The amount will be credited back to your Amazon balance immediately once we verify the cards. It's temporary and fully refundable.
Alright, I suppose I can go to the store. Should I call you back when I have them?
You can stay on the line if that's easier. Once you have the cards, I'll need the codes from the back to process the refund for you.
Okay, I'm heading out now. Please hold.
Of course, take your time. I'll stay with you to guide you through each step and answer any questions.
Alright, I got the cards. What do I do now?
Great job, Mrs. Matthews. Please carefully scratch off the metallic strip on each card and read me the numbers, starting with the first one.
Okay, here's the first code: 1234 5678 9001 2345.
Thank you. Now the second card, please.
And the last card?

Thank you, Mrs. Matthews. I'm processing your refund now. You should see the $299 credit on your Amazon balance soon. Please don't share these codes with anyone else, as they are linked directly to your refund.
Alright, I hope this works. I just can't afford to lose any more money.
You're in good hands. If you have further questions or see any other unfamiliar activity, just give us a call. Your account is now secure, and you don't need to worry.
